CiCheck.description:
One required check that is not passing, named so the `ci-fix` skill can

ClientIdentity.description:
Who connected; it grants nothing. A `kind` of [`MACHINE_CLIENT`] is
another Machine: every operation it sends runs here and is never sent on.

oneOf.description: The connection's first message; the server answers `welcome`.
A pre-hello readiness probe; the server answers `status` and closes.

A bridge's first and only message: the ticket `session.attach` issued.
The server answers `bridged`, and the connection then speaks the owner
protocol. A ticket opens one bridge, within [`TICKET_LIFETIME`], for the
user who requested it; otherwise the answer is `error` and the connection closes.

`id` is 1–128 bytes and unique among this connection's unanswered requests.
`select` keeps only those dotted paths of a read's answer (`task.title`;
a path through an array applies to each element, a missing path is
absent); null keeps it whole, and a write refuses one.

request_id.description:
Names one write across connections and restarts: for a day, a
repeat under the same ID gets the first answer and runs nothing; a
different operation under it is `invalid`. Null for reads and for
writes the client never repeats.

sender.description:
What the Machine that sent the request runs with; null from a
client on this Machine.

oneOf.description:
A read with a subscription; answers a null `response`, then `reading` messages
until cancelled. The id follows the same rules as a request's. `select`
is as for a request; a change outside it sends no reading.

resume.description: The last applied reading's opaque checkpoint; null starts fresh.

oneOf.description:
Ask the live subscription `id` for a reading now; the next reading's
`answers` carries `checkpoint`, changed or not.
Forget a request's answer, or end a subscription.

Close.description:
The last frame before an orderly terminal disconnect. No stream offset
transfers to a replacement terminal.

oneOf.description: The terminal attachment moved to a replacement. Reattach by Session.
Execution finished. Stop automatic reattachment.
Cleanup ended this terminal. Deliberate resume remains available.

builtin.description:

The Machine that runs it when another Machine than this one owns it;
`null` when this Machine owns it or nobody does.

selection_states.description: The same lifecycle, section and conversation activity states as selections.

RunDied.description: A Task run's carrier died while the run was at a step.

at.description: RFC 3339; `null` when nobody recorded the death.

at_step.description: The step the run reached, where it starts again.

Scope.description: One resolver reading for the selected work and each editable declaration.

read_path.description: Document supplying these slots, or the destination when no document exists.

slots.description: Includes absent slots. Omitted keys do not apply at this destination.

Secrets.description: Values by environment variable name; never logged.

Selection2.description: Who asks, and how: what a launch the request starts runs with.

participant.description: The name its person's Task claims carry.

profile.description: The sender's personal settings and definitions.

source.description: A shipped Task's branch and Linear mapping, which resolve here.

SelectionId.description: Stable authored node identity, independent of its position in a composition.

unavailable.description: Nonempty means departures cannot be inferred from this reading.

oneOf.description: Session axis: a Task conversation is available for the person's next turn.
Session axis: a current Task Session report says it is working.
Task axis: effective lifecycle, including withdrawal of never-started work.
Board axis: the Task's `TaskSection`.
Setting axis: the open Task's auto setting is on.

Sender.description:
What the Machine that sent a request runs with. An operation names the
sender's own directory; it runs in this Machine's checkout of `repository`.

client_id.description: The server's name for this connection, as `lf server status` lists it.

machine.description: Null while the Machine registry is unavailable or uninitialized.

revision.description: The revision both sides speak for this connection.

oneOf.description:
What the request returned: the value its operation's `x-result` names,
null once a subscription is confirmed. `trace_id` correlates the server's
diagnostics for it.

revisions.description:
For a write, each store domain it advanced, at its value after the
commit: a reading at or past every one shows the write. Null for
reads and server operations.

oneOf.description:
The answer to `attach`: the connection now speaks the viewer protocol
with this held terminal, and nothing more arrives from the server.
One subscription line; its `body` has the shape of the read's `x-result`.

checkpoint.description: Resume this reading on another connection to the same server.

oneOf.description:
The answer for `id` is `bytes` long, more than `limits.max_message`:
a ticketed connection delivers it as one message.
A ticketed connection's answer; what follows is what the ticket names.
Connection-local ordering; never a replay or reading checkpoint.

The subscription's last reading was its answer (`task.wait` reached
its state); nothing follows for `id`.
`id` is null before a request exists. An error for a subscription ends it.

data.description: Structured detail a client can act on, such as the missing resource.

revisions.description:
The domains that advanced while a failed write ran, by it or by
another write; null when none did.

ServerOperation.description: Operations the server owns rather than a shared read or write.

oneOf.description:
A ticket for the Session's held terminal, answered `{ticket,
terminal_id, expires_in_ms}`. A new connection presents the ticket as
its first message (`attach`) and becomes the bridge; this connection
stays a client. An orderly terminal sends a final `0x07` frame with
JSON `{reason: replaced|finished|retired}` (see `x-terminal-close`).
After `replaced`, attaching by the same Session reaches its next terminal.
Bare EOF leaves the reason unknown. A Session no terminal
runs is `not_found`; attaching never starts a provider. A Session
another Machine runs is attached there and bridged through here.

machine.description: For a Session with no Task here, the Machine that runs it.

task.description: The Session's Task: the server attaches wherever the Task runs.

terminal_id.description: Attach only to this held terminal.

oneOf.description:
Start the Session's agent in this build's holder and answer
`{terminal_id}`. `env` is the caller's whole environment; the server's
is not used. Repeating `request` answers the terminal it started.
This is the only operation here that creates a process.

placement.description:
The Desktop pane (`LF_TERMINAL_ID`) the caller's own terminal was
validated as; the held child continues it on its PTY. Null outside
a pane.

oneOf.description:
Continue an existing Session in a held terminal: `lf session resume`
of exactly `session`, in its directory, with the server's environment.
Answers `{terminal_id}`; repeating `request` answers the terminal it
started. For a client with no environment of its own to send. A
Session another Machine runs continues there.

agent.description:
The caller's `--agent` (`harness[:model]`): the Session continues on
it, importing its history when the harness differs. Null keeps the
Session's own.

machine.description: For a Session with no Task here, the Machine that runs it.

task.description: The Session's Task: the server attaches wherever the Task runs.

oneOf.description:
Start a Task shell in the checkout of the Machine that runs the Task
and answer `{terminal_id}`. `shell_id` names it there: repeating it
answers the same terminal and starts nothing. `command` runs first
after login startup; `bootstrap` is Desktop's Ghostty startup JSON.
A Task with no checkout is `not_found {reason: "not_started"}`.

A ticket for a Task shell's running terminal, like `session.attach`.
It never starts one: an ended or unknown shell is `not_found`. A shell
is named only on the Machine that started it.
Close a Task shell and end its terminal; answers `{}`.

machine.description:
The Machine that started the shell, which keeps it after the
Task moves; null closes it where the Task runs.

oneOf.description: Mobile access readiness; same-user local socket only.

x-result-example.error: Sign in to Tailscale on this Machine

oneOf.description:
Turn mobile access on with `configuration`, or off with null; same-user
local socket only. Answers `{configuration}`.

A ticket for a connection that carries one request of `bytes` bytes,
larger than `limits.max_message`; answers `{ticket}`. The uploaded
request is answered here under its own id.

A provider hook at a turn or tool boundary. The server records what the
boundary says (the native turn, the acknowledged input, `gap`) and
answers the Session's pending steers. At `stop` it answers first, then
refreshes planning and applies a pending Session move.

adapter.description:
The provider context the launch gave the agent; null for a
conversation lf did not start (a Codex app-server thread), whose
`stop` only refreshes planning.

callback.description: The JSON the provider sent the hook, unchanged.

gap.description:
The hook's open recording gap; the server writes it into the
Session's history as one `store-gap` observation.

inbox.description:
Where an idle conversation takes steers and Task updates: Claude's
inbox key, or an OpenCode or Pi work session's socket. Null from
Codex, a worker and a Claude with no inbox.

printed.description:
Unused: hooks claim their own steers from the store. Conversations
started before then still send it. TODO(LOO-838): delete it with
`ContextMoment::TaskUpdates`, once none of them is live.

oneOf.description:
The hub's side of a plan exchange: take in another Machine's stamped
records of `repository`'s plan, in one transaction. Each field is
written only when its stamp is newer than the one held here, so
repeating it changes nothing.

SessionAction.description:
What opening a Session does here, as a person reads it. Every opening is
`lf resume`: it adds a view, resumes saved history, or takes the
conversation over from a client lf can't share.

SessionAttached.description: What `session.attach` answers: a ticket that opens one bridge.

expires_in_ms.description: How long the ticket opens a bridge, from when it was issued.

terminal_id.description: The held terminal the bridge reaches.

SessionBindingPreview.description: Resolved identity for confirmation, not a reservation or permission to bind.

SessionBoundaryAnswer.description:
What `session.boundary` answers: nothing. Hooks claim their own steers and
Task update from the store. The three fields are what conversations
started before then still parse. TODO(LOO-838): delete them with
`ContextMoment::TaskUpdates`, once none of those conversations is live.

control_holder.description: The recorded occupied terminal, never an input-control credential.

last_line.description: Last nonempty line of the current provider preview, not terminal scrollback.

exit_code.description:
The provider's exit; `null` when nobody saw it (the holder died, or
the Machine restarted).

SessionGraphMembership.description:
Whether a Session's conversation is an occurrence of a Graph. Membership
comes only from its recorded Graph invocation, never from matching Task, checkout,
provider, or skill.

node.description: Exact graph occurrence, unavailable for older capture manifests.

SessionGraphOccurrence.description: Where a Graph occurrence sits relative to its Graph's current position.

oneOf.description: The row retains membership but no selected occurrence.
The invocation's current position.
An earlier position of the invocation that is still active.
An invocation that has finished.

skill_version.description: SHA-256 of the resolved skill text the run launched with; `null` when unrecorded.

SessionOrigin.description: The Machine a collected Session was read from.

SessionOutlook.description:
Whether a conversation that is not running comes up, and what brings it.
The server works this out; no client does it again from `ended` and
`start`.

at.description:
RFC 3339: when the server starts it next; a time already past is a
start under way. `null` when the server will not start it, and for
one that is starting.

command.description: The command that opens it; `null` while the server brings it up.

reason.description:
Ready to print. Why it could not start; for one coming back, that its
last start failed and why; for one waiting, why the server leaves it.

oneOf.description:
No agent runs yet and one is on its way: a Task's conversation the
server here is starting, or a start whose agent has no pid recorded.
It died and the server here starts it again, at `at`.

It is down and only its command brings it up: it is not a Task's
conversation, or the server here does not or no longer starts it.
The person quit it. It stays quit.

No agent has run yet: its start failed, for `reason`. The server
tries again at `at`, or left it to `command`.

SessionPreview.description: Bounded provider text observed on the current native turn. Display evidence only.

account.description: The login its conversation last ran on; absent for an unrouted one.

action.description: How opening it here reads; absent for a Run, which opens nowhere.

agent_process_id.description: The provider's current AgentProcess; absent when Loopflow never launched one.

availability.description:
Available for a person, judged from current stream or terminal reports; absent when it is
working or nothing current says.

ended.description:
How its last agent ended, while none runs; `null` for a headless
Session, before a first start, or when nobody recorded the end.

model.description: The model its current input launched with, when one was named.

outlook.description:
What happens next to a conversation that is not running, as this
Machine reads it; `null` while it runs, and when nothing says why it
is down.

provider.description:
The provider its current input launched with; absent until a review's
first launch records one.

raw.description:
A conversation open here that Loopflow never launched; `id` is the
provider's conversation ID and no Session records it.

start.description:
The server's starts of a Task's conversation since it last finished a
turn; `null` when it made none, and once the person quit.

status_line.description:
Whether it runs, how it ended and its outlook, as one sentence in this
Machine's local time: "died 12:01 (exit 137) · starting again". Every
client prints it as given; `null` for a headless Session.

turn.description: Its current or last turn while it is live; `null` when nothing says.

SessionStarts.description: What the server's recovery pass did for a Task conversation.

attempts.description: Starts since it last finished a turn.

oneOf.description: Passive metadata has no trustworthy live/closed observation.
Its agent runs, but no terminal shows it.

SessionTitleSource.description:
Who chose a Session's current title. A human name is never replaced by a
generated suggestion. `Unavailable` is never stored: the canonical name
lives on another Machine and the reader only has a local display label.

SessionTurn.description:
A conversation's current or last turn: a transcript `Turn` without what
was said in it.

id.description: The provider's name for the turn.

started_at.description: RFC 3339; absent when the turn began before what was read.

usage.description:
Tokens across the turn's model calls so far; absent when nothing
reports them.

SessionUsage.description:
Provider-authored cumulative usage reduced once per independent stream.

Optional counters stay unknown when no stream reported them. Finality is a
count of direct provider receipts; Recorder settlement never upgrades it.

SettingCandidate.description: All candidates are ordered from lowest to highest authority.

key.description: Authored key; agent and default_agent retain their choice strength.

SetupValue.description: One effective setting; `value` is absent when nothing chooses one.

SlotLayout.description:
A Dashboard page's fixed slots. Members fill slots by number, in order, and
overflow to further pages; they never add, remove or resize slots.

authors.description: Recorded steer authors. Empty for every other source.

count.description: Assets, steers, tool results or compactions; unknown when unrecorded.

SplitAxis.description: `vertical` places children side by side; `horizontal` stacks them.

SqlReceipt.description:
One evaluation can be shared by several subscriptions. Its identity lets
clients count that physical work once within an interaction.

Starter.description:
Who started a Process, derived from its ancestry: the first Session an
agent ran it from, else the person at the root of its chain.

oneOf.description:
A person ran it. `name` is absent when no participant is configured or
the chain is missing rows: attribution unresolved.
An agent in this Session ran it, for its person.
A configured default set it: `auto: on`. Only an auto mark names one.

StatusRecorded.description: The snapshot a Session's Program Status now holds.

SteerAdapter.description: Belongs to one agent; replacement creates another capability.

SteerReached.description: Where the steer has been saved so far.

assembled_tokens.description: Everything Loopflow assembled and submitted, in cl100k tokens.

first_request_tokens.description: Input the provider reported for its first and largest requests.

SubscriptionEvent.description: An occurrence within the Tasks included in a subscription reading.

comment.description: The thread entry when this direction came from a retained comment.

answers.description: The newest request this reading began after.

read_at.description:
Every store domain's revision in the snapshot this reading used; null
without a store. A write whose answered revisions this reaches shows here.

unavailable.description: Why the read failed. `body` is then `null`.

oneOf.description: `preview`: the strategy a sync would take; nothing moved.
The sync runs detached as `process`, with its output in `log`.
The sync, continue or abort finished in place.

fork_base.description: The recorded stack base shared by planning, integration and the PR range.

head.description: The commit the plan classified; the sync refuses if HEAD moved since.

TailscaleIdentity.description: A device's Tailscale identity, as `tailscale status` and `whois` report it.

user.description: The Tailscale user ID that owns the device.

parent_task_id.description:
The Task this one was filed from; its children are the Tasks naming it.
Not the stack: `parent_pr_id` says which branch it starts from.

rank.description: Shared planning fields; independent of local execution and Workflow position.

repo_id.description: Stable repository identity, independent of planning membership.

revision.description: Local optimistic-write revision; independent of Linear observation age.

state.description: Linear's state type, `completed` once done; the lifecycle is `TaskState`.

tracker_id.description: The record’s ID in the repository's tracker.

tracker_synced_at.description: Time of the last successful tracker refresh.

wave_id.description: Read projection from the Project join, validated against the Project on save.

changes.description:
Runs of changed lines in the file's patch, each the Diff's stop: a run
ends at an unchanged line, a hunk's end, or a removal after additions.

commits.description:
The commits on head's first-parent line since base, oldest first,
without merges.

TaskChecks.description: Recorded required checks, pinned to the observed PR head. Null means unobserved.

TaskComments.description:
The saved Task thread, its pending deliveries and any failed refresh.
Partial provider reads never replace the retained thread.

conflicts.description: Losing local comment bodies; the thread contains the adopted Linear values.

TaskCommit.description:
One commit in a Task's comparison. A Graph step's commits share the subject
prefix `lf <step>:`.

parent.description: The commit's first parent: a step starting here compares against it.

TaskCompleted.description:
`lf task complete --json`: the completed Task and what its completion did
with each child. Wire type; no defaults.

children.description:
One entry per Task filed from it that was open, in the order the
command prints them.

parent_task_id.description:
The Task this one was filed from; its children are the Tasks naming it.
Not the stack: `parent_pr_id` says which branch it starts from.

rank.description: Shared planning fields; independent of local execution and Workflow position.

repo_id.description: Stable repository identity, independent of planning membership.

revision.description: Local optimistic-write revision; independent of Linear observation age.

state.description: Linear's state type, `completed` once done; the lifecycle is `TaskState`.

tracker_id.description: The record’s ID in the repository's tracker.

tracker_synced_at.description: Time of the last successful tracker refresh.

wave_id.description: Read projection from the Project join, validated against the Project on save.

TaskConditionSnapshot.description: A Task's shared condition and the evidence that proves it.

evidence_age_secs.description: Age of the durable Work evidence at that sample, if Work exists.

observed_at.description: RFC3339 time local workspace evidence was sampled.

unresolved_execution.description:
Started work a finished plan has not settled: the Task is still ready,
its Graph is not idle, or its checkout holds observed unsettled work.
Keeps a terminal Task in the working set.

TaskConditionState.description:
A Task's derived operating condition. Sessions own review actions; this state
only lets Work surfaces explain whether the Task is clear, waiting on
another actor, blocked, or unreadable.

TaskCreated.description:
`task.create`'s answer: its receipt, the primary conversation's record, the
Task's parent and its row in the Work projection's shape, read when answering, so a
client selects the Task and opens the conversation before its planning
subscription lists it. The stored receipt holds neither.

parent.description: The Task this one was filed from; `null` for top-level work.

oneOf.description: Historical authored direction; the immutable publication owns its text.

A request to end the Task's current turn so the next one re-reads its
direction immediately. A live run acts on interrupts issued after it
launched; there is nothing to interrupt otherwise. Not a report out.

History only: an earlier `lf task complete` that would settle the
Task's children once it ran. Completion now settles children at once,
by the policy given, and nothing writes this.

captured.description: The Session input that step captured, when it opened one.

died.description:
Where the run's carrier (`lf task run`) died before the run stopped;
`null` for a run that runs, stopped on its own, or never started.

outlook.description:
What happens next to a run that died, as this Machine reads it: the
server here starts it again at `at`, or leaves it to `command` for
`reason`. `null` unless `died` says it did.

step.description: Label of the latest Graph's latest step, while that Graph is unfinished.

oneOf.description:
Its step is waiting out a usage limit until an account frees up, or
its run waits to be carried again after its carrier died.

data.description: A `binary` file's bytes, base64, up to `MAX_BINARY_DATA_BYTES`.

TaskFilesRevision.description:
A Task's file invalidation on this Machine. `checkout` and `revision` are
null until the Task has a checkout here; readers rescan on a new revision,
including when multiple changes coalesce while their connection is busy.

TaskFollowUp.description: Historical keep-open scope, retained for event decoding only.

TaskGraph.description: One Task's Graph as `lf task status --json` carries it.

current_step.description:
The index in `steps` of the step the Task stands in; null at `start`
and at `end`.

sentence.description:
Where the Task stands, in one sentence: "build is running implement.
You are next needed at ship-review."

steps.description: The Graph's top-level steps in order, as the workflow line shows them.

oneOf.description:
The Task stands at `start`, at `end`, or at this interactive step,
waiting on a person in the Task conversation.

`lf task run` (`lf_process_id`) carries the Task on from `step`, and
runs `at`. `running` is read from that Process: a run that ended
without arriving stopped, and the next `lf task run` starts it again
at `at`; the steps before it stay done.

TaskOverview.description: Workspace facts without the Task's full history.

person_id.description: The person's `people` id, where the entry named one.

TaskOwnership.description:
This Machine's reading of a Task's ownership. `superseded_by` names a later
claim that every other Machine follows while this Machine keeps its own.

machine_label.description: The Machine's label when written, or as best known on this Machine.

order.description:
Where the entry sorts in the Task's log on every Machine, from its
writer's plan clock. Absent with Linear or Asana, whose comment order
decides, and from entries written before claims were first-wins.

person_id.description:
The person's `people` id, their tracker's identity for them.
Absent from entries released lf wrote and where the writer knew none.

person_key.description: The person's stable key; names are display only.

seen.description:
The entry in effect when this one was written, or this entry itself
when there was none. Present exactly when `order` is. A claim whose
writer had not seen the claim holding the Task loses to it.

writer_machine_id.description: Absent from entries lf before `task_machine_local` wrote, which name no writer.

ci_observation.description:
The most recent required-check reading for this PR's open head. `None`
until the head has been observed; ignored once the head moves past
`CiObservation::head_sha`.

github_observation.description:
Last GitHub refresh attempt. A fresh result coalesces reads briefly; a
degraded result opens a longer circuit while the durable PR fields stand.

linear_attachment_id.description:
Id of the first-class Linear attachment linking this PR on its owning
issue. `None` until the PR is first published; carried forward so later
publishes update the same attachment in place.

linear_comment_id.description:
Id of the loopflow-managed Linear comment carrying the PR URL and state.
Its presence switches the writeback from `commentCreate` to `commentUpdate`.

linear_link_error.description:
`None` when the last Linear linkage writeback succeeded; the last error
string when it degraded. The GitHub publication still succeeded — this only
records that the Linear side is behind, and is cleared on the next success.

parent_pr_id.description:
Selected parent PR, or `None` when rooted on the default branch.
Selection does not move Git: `base_commit` remains the child's last
recorded fork until sync succeeds. The link clears after the parent
merges and this PR collapses onto main.

TaskReferenceSnapshot.description:
Stable references for one Task, shared verbatim by `lf wave status` and
`lf wave show`. The issue URL is cached PM evidence. Workspace evidence comes
from the durable Task and outlives its execution and final PR.

TaskRow.description: One Task. Wire type; no defaults.

next.description:
The command that moves it on; `null` while it moves by itself, runs on
another Machine or is closed.

parent_id.description: The `id` of the Task this one was filed from; `null` for top-level work.

project.description: Its Project's name; `null` outside any Project.

reason.description: Why it is in that state, or what it waits on.

runs_on.description:
The Machine that runs it when another Machine than this one owns it;
`null` when this Machine owns it or nobody does.

state.description: `null` when live execution is on another Machine and was not read.

wave.description: Its Wave's name; `null` outside any Wave.

step.description: The step it stands at (`start`, `end` or an interactive step); `null` while a run carries it.

oneOf.description: The run's Graph process registered; it goes on without its launcher.

log.description:
Where the run's output goes once its launcher lets go; null while a
terminal (`-b`, `-i`) keeps it.

merges.description:
The run may merge the PR: auto is on, or no interactive step is
left ahead, and nobody turned auto off.

run.description: The graph and where the run set out: `code from implement`.

oneOf.description: Nothing runs: the Task now waits at this interactive step.
Nothing remained: the Task is at `end`.

TaskRunsOn.description:
The Machine that runs a Task another Machine owns, and since when: the
latest ownership entry naming it. Wire type; no defaults.

machine.description:
Named as this Machine's preferences name it, else as the claim
published it, else by its id.

completion_pending.description: A durable completion request awaiting settlement.

owner.description:
Who owns the Task on which Machine, as this Machine reads the ownership
log; absent when the Task is unowned.

status.description: Completion and abandonment are independent of Graph position.

TaskSection.description:
Where a Task sits on the Wave board. The one bucketing rule: the board, the
sidebar's Working Tasks, Wave counts and `lf wave show` all read it.

oneOf.description: Waiting for someone to pick it up: unstarted, or started and unassigned.
Someone's idle, active or moving Task, or a Task owned on another Machine.

TaskSession.description: Conversation identity and completion, without loading its input or transcript.

graph_lf_process_id.description: The Graph whose step opened its current input.

auto.description:
The Task's auto setting: on, off, and who set it when;
`null` when nobody has.

completion_pending.description: A durable completion request awaiting settlement.

observation.description:
Freshness of the PR state against GitHub as of this read. `Degraded`
means a bounded remote read failed and the PR fields are cached, not
freshly confirmed.

stack_parent.description: The Task this one is stacked on.

started_by.description: Who started the Task's latest Graph.

status.description: Completion and abandonment are independent of the Task's Graph position.

TaskStackParent.description: The Task a stacked Task builds on, as people name it.

pr_number.description: `None` until the parent opens its PR.

TaskState.description:
A Task's state, derived from its checkout, Graph position, whether a
Graph runs for it. Completion and abandonment
are durable; the open states follow what the Task is doing now. Whether
anyone owns it is ownership, not state.

oneOf.description: No checkout yet.

A checkout, no Graph running and not at an interactive step: before its first run,
or after a stopped one.
Between Graphs at an interactive step, in a conversation in its Task Session.

A Graph runs for it. Its auto setting says whether the run stands in
at interactive steps or stops there for a person.
Completed independently of Graph position.

parent_id.description: The stable ID of the Task this one was filed from.

oneOf.description: Its PR is open, or it finished first.
It is done or abandoned.

TaskWork.description: All retained work in a checkout, plus explicitly attributed work elsewhere.

graph.description: The graph the Task took up; `None` until its first `lf task run`.

local_exists.description: Existence on the reading Machine; unknown when the filesystem check fails.

ThemeDeclaration.description: The same theme declaration read by the phone, with its exact slot for Desktop edits.

TrackerActionStatus.description: One tracker action as a person reads it.

change.description: What changes, as a person names it: `title`, `complete`, `comment`.

error.description: Why the last request did not confirm it.

local_value.description: The value saved here; when conflicted, the one that lost.

seq.description: Send order across the repository; none for Git, which keeps no queue.

subject.description: The field or comment the change addresses.

tracker_value.description: The tracker's winning value, when conflicted.

TrackerKind.description: The tracker a queued planning change goes to.

TrackerState.description: The tracker's last known state for a Task and when it was synced.

TrackerStatus.description:
What `repo.tracker` answers: the tracker, or for a repository without
one how its plan travels, and every open and lost tracker action.

actions.description:
What the tracker has yet to confirm (open: `queued`, `sent`), in send
order, and each value it kept over a local one (lost: `conflicted`)
until it is answered.

plan.description: How a plan without a tracker travels; `null` with a tracker.

tracker.description: `linear` or `asana`; `null` when the plan is in Loopflow's store.

TrackerSync.description:
A Task's or Project's slice of `lf repo tracker`'s actions: what its tracker
has yet to confirm (open), and each value the tracker won (lost) until it
is answered.
Read-only; these rows never confer execution authority.

TurnUsage.description: `input_tokens` counts every input token, cached ones included.

Untyped.description: Untyped on the wire: any JSON value, with no shape promised.

argv.description: An explicit connect command, never a fallback shell or provider launch argv.

graph_step.description:
Where this Task stands on its captured Graph, including a running step.
Older Machines omit this field.

identifier.description: A Task's short name, as people say it: `LOO-809`.

open_children.description:
How many direct children of a Task are open, so a client can ask what
happens to them before completing it; `None` for anything but a Task.

ViewPlan.description: A passive host plan. It describes saved intent and observed Work, not native readiness.

repo_path.description:
The repository's canonical path on this Machine; its last component is
the name people see.

slots.description: The page geometry visible members fill, in projection order.

viewer.description:
Who a Claim run on this Machine names as owner; `None` without a Git
`user.email` in the repository, which claiming needs.

Waited.description: One reading of `task.wait`: the Task now, and whether it reached the state waited for.

WaveAdded.description:
`lf wave add --json`: the receipt Desktop and the CLI both show. `summary`
holds what is left to do after the add, one sentence per line; empty when
nothing is.

WaveDetailSnapshot.description:
`lf wave status <wave>` and `lf wave plan <wave>`: current planning,
Task conditions and Session history. Wire type; no defaults.

history.description: This Wave's Machine-local Session history, newest first.

project.description: The Wave's one Project; `None` for a Wave that has made none yet.

setup.description: What the Wave's Tasks run, where, and which logins pay, with each source.

WaveGraph.description:
The graph a scope's new Tasks take up, resolved through your `lf set wave.graph`,
the Wave's and the repository's `graph:`, then `code`.
The repository scope has no Wave.

WaveRemoval.description: The preview Desktop and the CLI render before removal, and the receipt after.

destination.description: Where open Tasks go: the parent Wave, or the repository when `None`.

uncommitted.description:
Files under `.lf/wave/<name>` with edits nobody committed on the main
checkout; removal deletes them with the directory, and Git keeps no copy.

waves.description: The Wave and every child Wave that retires with it.

WaveRenamed.description:
`lf wave rename --json`: the receipt Desktop and the CLI both show. `summary`
holds what is left to do after the rename, one sentence per line; empty when
nothing is.

graph.description: The graph the Wave's Tasks take up by default.

project.description: The Wave's one Project; `None` for a Wave that has made none yet.

auto.description: `on` when the Wave's Tasks turn auto on as they take up their Graph.

skill_agents.description: Agent by skill name, for every skill some layer names.

tasks_machine.description: Where the Wave's new Tasks run.

WaveSnapshot.description:
One wave's registry snapshot — the `lf wave list` row and the `wave` field of
`lf wave status`. Wire type consumed by Loopflow: every field is required or
explicitly Optional, no serde defaults.

active_tasks.description: Non-terminal Tasks owned by this Wave.

created_at.description: RFC3339 creation time, `null` when the row predates the column.

machine.description: Local execution placement and its route; absent for unplaced planning.

parent_wave_id.description: Parent wave id in the chord tree, `null` for a root wave.

retired_at.description: Tombstone time for stable-id history; active locator reads exclude it.

status.description: Current planning lifecycle derived from stable Work and concrete facts.

client_id.description: The server's name for this connection, as `lf server status` lists it.

machine.description: Null while the Machine registry is unavailable or uninitialized.

revision.description: The revision both sides speak for this connection.

subject.description: Current display label: Wave name, Project slug, or Task identifier.

truncated.description: More Session records exist in the window than `--limit` returned.

oneOf.description: An interrupt was recorded; `target` says what it reached and how.
Nothing was live, so nothing was recorded.

WorkLink.description: A readable, activatable Work link. Printing one opens nothing.

execution_machine.description: The execution owner when it is another Machine.

session.description: An explicit Session selection; ordinary Work links leave it absent.

task.description: The Task's readable identifier, such as LOO-507.

WorkSource.description: How this attempt received its work attribution; absent for unrecorded history.

repository.description: Durable repository plan ID, not a filesystem opening or execution locator.

WorkflowOutline.description: A Graph as the workflow line shows it before any Task stands on it.

interactive_steps.description: Every step where a person takes part, as `TaskGraph` carries them.

sentence.description: "You take part at explore, ship-review and verify." or "Runs on its own."

steps.description: The Graph's top-level steps in order, as `TaskGraph.steps` carries them.

WorkflowStep.description: One top-level step of a Task's Graph.

interactive.description: A person takes part somewhere inside it, XOR paths included.

oneOf.description: File or adopt a Task, with a durable request identity; optionally start it.

parent.description: The Task this one is filed from, by ID or identifier; `null` files top-level.

oneOf.description: `lf task complete <issue> [--children rehome|abandon]`.

children.description: What happens to open children; `null` refuses while any are open.

oneOf.description: `lf task reopen <issue>`.

`lf task edit <issue> [--notes=<notes>] [--rank=<rank>]`: a new brief,
a new position in its Project, or both.

`lf task abandon <issue>`: cancels the Task and removes its PRs and
branches.
`lf task claim <issue> --json`.
`lf task unassign <issue> --json`.

`lf [-b] [-a <agent>] task run <issue> [--from <step>] --json`, started
detached: the Graph process it started, or where the Task now waits.
`approve` is `-b`: every step headless to `end`; it writes no auto.

`lf task auto on <issue> --json`, started detached: turns auto on and returns the run, as
`task.run` does. Nothing else turns auto on.
`lf task auto off <issue> --json`: turns the Task's auto setting off.

reason.description: Why, saved as a comment on the Task.

oneOf.description:
`lf task sync <issue> [--keep-theirs | --use-mine]`: exchange the
Task with its tracker now, first answering every value it lost.
Answers what the command prints.

`lf repo tracker answer <action> --keep-theirs | --use-mine`: answer one
lost line of the directory's repository, whoever owns it. Answers the
line as it stood.

`lf steer <issue> <message> --json`: direction for the Task's
runs, whoever writes it.

`lf task report <issue> <message> --json`: progress for the Task's
thread; an agent's carries its Session's provenance.
`lf task interrupt <issue> --json`.
`lf task move <issue> --wave <wave>`, or `--no-wave` without one.

x-result.description: Moving a Task changes its Wave membership or its Machine ownership.

oneOf.description:
`lf task save <issue> <path> --revision <revision> --json`, with
`content` on stdin.

`lf [--wave <wave>] steer [<id>] <message> --json`: a steer
one Session, every Session of the Wave or, with neither, every Session
of the repository reads at its next boundary.
`lf session rename --json -- <id> <name>`.

action.help: Open this Session in a terminal
action.label: Open here

oneOf.description:
`lf session observe-status --json <id> --terminal <terminal> --stream
<stream> --sequence <n> [--agent-process <id>]`, `records` on stdin: one
Program Status reading from the terminal showing the Session.

`lf session bind --json --task <task> -- <id>`; with `preview`,
`--dry-run`: the Task a bind would assign, assigning nothing.

`lf [--agent <agent>] session resume [<id>] [--task <task>] [--wave <wave>]
--prepare --json`, with `--repo <directory>` when it names none of them:
the conversation and the command that opens it, no provider started.

`lf [--agent <agent>] session new <id> --prepare --json`: the
conversation on a fresh provider thread, not yet started.

task.description: The Task whose conversation this is; it is prepared where that Task runs.

oneOf.description:
`lf --agent <agent> session move --all --on <harness[:model]>
--json`: the open Sessions the selector names continue on the agent;
the report says which moved, which move after their turn, and which
were skipped.

`lf wave create <wave> [--objective <objective>] --json`: the Wave and
its authored files; an existing Wave is unchanged.
`lf wave sync <wave> --json`: the planning refresh.

`lf wave plan connect [<wave> [<project>]|--all] [--team-key <key>]
[--team-name <name>] --json`: one receipt per Wave connected.

`lf wave plan reteam [--apply] --json`: the moves onto the
repository's Team; a plan without `apply`.

`lf graph customize <name>`: copies a builtin Graph into the repository,
recording nothing.

`lf repo release run [<version>] [-t <target>] --json`, started
detached: the Process carrying the release.
`lf [-a <agent>] commit [-m <message>] [--no-push] [--no-add] [<path>…] --json`.

`lf sync [<onto>] [--plan|--manual|--continue|--abort] [--adopt]
--json`: the plan, a finished continue or abort, or the Process
carrying a sync started detached.
`lf wt create <name> [--plan] [--persistent] [--stack] --json`.

`lf -b [--agent <agent>] graph <name> [message]`, started detached: the
Process carrying the Graph.

`lf -b [--agent <agent>] skill <name> [message]`, started detached: the
Process carrying the skill's headless run.

`lf [--agent <agent>] pr publish [--title] [--body] --json`: push and
create or refresh the checkout's ready PR.

`lf [--agent <agent>] pr open [--title] [--body] --json`: push and
create or refresh the checkout's draft PR; served, no review surface
opens.

`lf [--agent <agent>] pr submit [--strict] [--worktree] [--message]
[--title] [--body] --json`: prepare the PR for a teammate's merge.

`lf [--agent <agent>] pr arm [--strict] [--local] [--worktree]
[--message] [--title] [--body] --json`: arm exact-head auto-merge and
return.

`lf [--agent <agent>] pr land [--wait-and-fix] [--strict] [--local]
[--worktree] [--message] [--title] [--body] --json`, started
detached: the Process carrying the landing.

`lf pr abandon [<branch>] [--force] --json`: close the PR and delete
its worktree and branches. Served, unpublished work is deleted only
with `force`.

`lf pr reconcile --json`: check recorded landings once and settle
verified merges.
`lf pr request-review [<pr>] -r <reviewer>… --json`.

`lf desktop portfolio <change> --json`, run from `/`: which
repositories the app shows.
`lf desktop dashboard query [--revision <revision>] -- <id> <expression>`.
`lf desktop dashboard pin <id> --revision <revision>`.
`lf desktop dashboard unpin <id> --revision <revision>`.
`lf desktop dashboard rename --revision <revision> -- query:<id> <name>`.
`lf desktop dashboard hide query:<id>/<member>`.
`lf desktop dashboard show query:<id>/<member>`.

`lf desktop dashboard slots query:<id> --revision <revision>`, with
`slots` (JSON) on stdin.

`lf desktop dashboard move <board>/<member> --destination <destination>`:
move to the target's slot, or place the member on its chosen side with `--side before|after`.

`lf config set <key> <value> <destination flags> --json`: declare a
setting in the destination's file; `value` is YAML.

`lf config unset <key> <destination flags> --json`: remove that
declaration so other sources choose.
Change a catalog setting if its authored declarations still match.
Preview a checked edit against the current configuration file.
Preview, confirm or undo a move to the next broader configuration file.

The Machine's `theme:` choice: set to `value`, or read when null.
Desktop owns its Apply/Cancel transaction and the phone reads it; no
CLI spells it.
